papers.title: DZIKR AND MEDITATION IN TASHAWWUF: Spiritual Disciplines, Psychological Benefits, and Their Contemporary Relevance
papers.abstract: Dzikr (remembrance of Allah) and meditation are core spiritual practices in Islam that support inner peace and personal transformation. Grounded in the Qur’an and developed within tashawwuf (Sufism), they aim to purify the self (tazkiyah al-nafs), deepen God-consciousness, and cultivate spiritual tranquillity. This study explores the relevance of dzikr and meditation by integrating Islamic spiritual perspectives with contemporary psychological and mental-health insights. Using a qualitative–descriptive method, data were obtained through literature analysis and participatory observation in dzikr and meditation gatherings, supplemented by informal interviews. The results show that these practices enhance spiritual well-being by fostering gratitude, emotional balance, and awareness of the Divine, while also producing measurable psychological benefits such as reduced stress and increased resilience. The study concludes that dzikr and meditation remain highly relevant for promoting holistic well-being and providing accessible pathways to balance and meaning in modern life.

papers.title: Mindfulness oasis: Cultivating mental wellness through Zen meditation retreats for tourists with mental and psychological vulnerabilities
Escaping the Self-Repair Trap: Improving Test Oracle Generation via Dual-Context Awareness
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown strong potential for regression-oracle completion, where a test prefix is given and the current program version is treated as expected behavior. Recent approaches increasingly rely on iterative self-repair and execution feedback, but optimizing execution success does not necessarily yield strong fault-revealing oracles. This objective, widely adopted in repair-based methods, serves only as a proxy and may be misaligned with the true goal of oracle generation. Such misalignment biases the repair process, giving rise to a feedback-driven degeneration that we term the Self-Repair Trap, where iterative repair progressively drives models toward assertions that are easier to satisfy but less effective at detecting faults. To address this issue, we propose DCAware, a computationally efficient, non-iterative framework that prioritizes high signal-to-noise contextual grounding over multi-round repair. DCAware integrates structured static context with selectively retrieved dynamic states, enabling precise and robust oracle generation without iterative feedback loops. Extensive experiments based on execution and mutation testing show that DCAware consistently improves fault-revealing effectiveness while maintaining high execution success, outperforming prior methods with substantially lower computational cost. Our results suggest that improving contextual quality is more effective than adding iterative repair complexity in the studied regression-oracle setting.

papers.title: Five Hundred Monks in Crisis: Meditation-Related Difficulties and Prescriptive Responses in the Pāli Commentarial Tradition
papers.abstract: Meditation-related difficulties have been systematically documented in contemporary contemplative science, yet the prescriptive resources preserved in the ancient Buddhist commentarial literature remain underutilized in comparative research. This study analyzes the case of five hundred monks in the Paramatthajotikā I’s commentary on the Karaṇīya-metta-sutta. During intensive practice, these monks experienced complex psychosomatic symptoms—perceptual disturbances, fear, somatic distress, and cognitive impairment—and received from the Buddha an integrated prescription of five protective practices (pañca rakkhā). Through Pāli textual and comparative analysis with Lindahl et al.’s taxonomy of meditation-related difficulties, this study demonstrates that the monks’ symptoms correspond systematically to the perceptual, affective, somatic, and cognitive domains of the modern taxonomy, with the critical difference residing in interpretive frameworks rather than in the phenomena themselves. The five practices—loving-kindness meditation, protective chant recitation, contemplation of impurity, mindfulness of death, and the arousal of religious urgency—constitute a sequentially structured system progressing from the emotional reframing of fear to the deconstruction of bodily and existential attachment, culminating in the restoration of soteriological motivation. This study argues that Paramatthajotikā I’s prescriptive system provides a historically grounded, soteriologically oriented complement to contemporary contemplative science, particularly in bridging the gap between phenomenological classification and meaning-centered intervention.

papers.title: Pengaruh Meditasi Mindfulness terhadap Penurunan Tingkat Kecemasan (Anxiety)Anxiety atau gangguan kecemasan merupakan salah satu masalah kesehatan mental yang banyak dialami oleh masyarakat modern, baik laki-laki maupun perempuan, terutama pada era digita
papers.abstract: Anxiety or anxiety disorders are among the most prevalent mental health problems experienced by modern society, affecting both men and women, particularly in the digital era due to pressures from family, work, academic demands, and social environments. One non-pharmacological approach that is widely used to address anxiety disorders is mindfulness meditation. This article aims to examine conceptually and empirically the effect of mindfulness meditation on reducing anxiety levels. The method employed is a literature review of relevant national journals. The findings indicate that consistent practice of mindfulness meditation is effective in reducing anxiety symptoms through increased self-awareness, improved emotional regulation, and greater acceptance of unpleasant experiences. Therefore, mindfulness meditation can be recommended as a complementary intervention in the management of anxiety disorders

papers.title: A scoping literature review of factors associated with burnout among student pharmacists in the United States.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Burnout is an increasing challenge among student pharmacists. Individual studies have examined burnout among student pharmacists; however, faculty and college administrators lack a consolidated understanding of the educational, personal, and contextual factors associated with burnout. This scoping literature review explored factors associated with burnout among student pharmacists in the United States. METHODS: For this scoping literature review, MEDLINE, Scopus, Embase, and PsycINFO were searched for English-language studies published between January 2000 and February 2026. Records were deduplicated in EndNote and Covidence. Eligible studies reported factors associated with burnout or related outcomes, including emotional exhaustion, anxiety, depression, and poor well-being. Quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies were included. Two independent reviewers screened studies, assessed full texts, and extracted data, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR guidelines. RESULTS: Eleven studies met the inclusion criteria from 2893 screened records. Most were published since 2020, used observational survey designs, and included students from one or more United States colleges of pharmacy. Validated burnout measures, primarily the Maslach Burnout Inventory and Oldenburg Burnout Inventory, were commonly used. Burnout was associated with intrinsic program factors (year in program, workload, competitive culture, campus assignment), extrinsic factors (co-curricular activities, employment, career planning), and individual factors (sex, marital status, sleep, nutrition, resilience, lack of time). One randomized trial found a mindfulness application reduced burnout after six weeks, although longer-term effects were mixed. CONCLUSION: Burnout requires systemic curricular reform, integrated wellness initiatives, and longitudinal, multi-institutional research to improve student well-being and reduce burnout.

papers.title: ReBAN-Net: An interpretable hybrid deep learning framework for ECG-based emotion recognition.
papers.abstract: Emotional assessment is essential for mental health management, yet questionnaire-based scales are subjective and facial- or voice-based approaches can be influenced by intentional behavior and environmental interference. This study proposes ReBAN-Net, a hybrid architecture integrating a one-dimensional residual convolutional network, a bidirectional long short-term memory network, and a soft attention mechanism for ECG-based emotion recognition. Three classification tasks were defined throughout the study: nine-class valence classification (levels 1-9), nine-class arousal classification (levels 1-9), and four-class affective-state classification (baseline, stress, amusement, and meditation). The model was evaluated on the WESAD dataset using a strict 15-fold leave-one-subject-out protocol. It achieved accuracies of 86.03% for nine-class valence, 86.27% for nine-class arousal, and 87.58% for four-class affective-state classification, with corresponding macro-AUC values of 96.07%, 96.24%, and 95.09%. Temporal class activation and attention-feature analyses show that the model focuses on physiologically meaningful ECG regions. These results demonstrate the feasibility and interpretability of ReBAN-Net and indicate its potential for subject-independent ECG-based emotion recognition.

papers.title: From trauma to words: the effect of bibliotherapy on psychological flexibility and language skills in children affected by an earthquake.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: The 6 February 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes caused widespread devastation across 11 provinces in southeastern Türkiye, resulting in profound psychosocial consequences for children, including increased emotional avoidance and difficulties in self-expression. This study aimed to examine changes in psychological flexibility and language-related outcomes (listening, speaking, reading comprehension, and writing) associated with participation in a bibliotherapy-based intervention among children affected by the earthquakes. METHODS: The study employed a quasi-experimental pretest-posttest control group design. Participants were middle school students residing in the earthquake-affected region. The experimental group participated in a 12-week multicomponent ACT-based bibliotherapy program, whereas the control group continued with the regular educational curriculum. The intervention was structured around Russ Harris's The Reality Slap and incorporated guided reading, metaphor-based activities, mindfulness practices, reflective writing, and group discussions. Each session involved structured reading of designated chapters and page ranges aligned with the thematic focus and targeted ACT processes. Psychological flexibility and four language-related outcomes-listening, speaking, reading comprehension, and writing-were assessed at pretest and posttest. RESULTS: Significant differential changes were observed for psychological flexibility and reading comprehension. For listening, the primary Time × Group interaction reached the conventional 0.05 significance level but did not remain statistically significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas the baseline-adjusted ANCOVA showed a statistically significant between-group difference (p = 0.008). Thus, the findings for listening were not consistent across analytical approaches and were interpreted cautiously. The Time × Group interactions for speaking and writing were not statistically significant. CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that participation in the multicomponent ACT-based bibliotherapy program was associated with improvements in psychological flexibility and reading comprehension among earthquake-affected adolescents. Evidence for listening skills was less consistent across analytical approaches and should therefore be interpreted cautiously. Given the quasi-experimental design, nonrandom allocation, and absence of an attention-matched active control condition, these findings should not be interpreted as definitive causal effects attributable exclusively to bibliotherapy.

papers.title: Yoga Effect on Quality of Life Study Among Patients with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (YES-IPF).
papers.abstract: RATIONALE: Patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) have poor health-related quality of life. OBJECTIVE: To explore the feasibility and potential impact of a modified yoga program on health-related quality of life in patients with IPF compared with usual care. METHODS: We conducted a randomized, controlled, nonblinded, 12-week pilot clinical trial with two arms involving 63 adults with IPF diagnosed according to the 2018 ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT clinical practice guideline. The yoga arm attended one-hour virtual group sessions twice weekly for 12 weeks, consisting of seated postures, breathing exercises, and meditation designed for patients with IPF, while the control arm continued usual care. MEASURE: ments: Health-related quality of life was assessed using seven patient-reported outcome measures and their associated domains. RESULTS: Sixty of 63 randomized participants completed the week-12 assessment and comprised the analysis cohort; their mean age was 73.4 years (SD, 8.2). Statistically significant improvements favoring yoga were seen in the Living with Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (L-IPF) cough domain (-9.29 points, 95% CI -18.37 to -0.20; p=0.045; SMD=-0.36), the L-IPF total score (-7.11, 95% CI -13.15 to -1.06; p=0.022; SMD=-0.38), and the R-scale-PF cough domain (-1.18, 95% CI -2.27 to -0.10; p=0.034; SMD=-0.45). CONCLUSION: In this exploratory pilot trial, a modified yoga program was feasible and well tolerated and was associated with improvements in selected patient-reported outcome domains. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant evaluation in a larger, adequately powered trial.

papers.title: 12-week yoga intervention effect on metabolome in Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS): An LC-MS-based study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a complex, heterogeneous disorder affecting endocrine, reproductive, and metabolic health. It is fundamentally a systemic metabolic defect that, if not addressed in time, can compromise the function of multiple systems, resulting in conditions such as impaired glucose tolerance, insulin resistance, cardiovascular disease, dyslipidemia, fatty liver disease, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. It is a lifestyle disorder with long-term health implications, requiring a holistic approach for management. METHODS: This prospective quasi-experimental study involved 60 women (30 diagnosed with PMOS, 30 age and BMI-matched controls). Women with PMOS underwent a 12-week Yoga practice that included physical postures (Asanas), regulated breathing practice (Pranayama), and meditation (Dhyana) under the guidance of a trained therapist. Clinical characteristics and laboratory biochemical data were recorded, followed by an untargeted metabolomics analysis using high-resolution Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid Mass Spectrometer technology to study plasma metabolome changes. RESULTS: Following Yoga intervention, women with PMOS showed significant improvements in hormonal, anthropometric parameters, and lipid profile. The metabolomics analysis showed that post-Yoga intervention, several key metabolites were significantly downregulated, including glucose, fructose, d-ribose, 3-hydroxybutanoate, taurine, and methylmalonate. However, metabolites like succinate and ascorbate were upregulated. Besides, AUC suggests significant metabolic shifts following Yoga intervention. CONCLUSION: Yoga offers a holistic, integrated mind-body approach to managing the endocrine, metabolic, and reproductive dysfunction in PMOS and lowers the risk of developing long-term comorbidities.
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine

papers.title: Religiosity and spirituality as stressors or stress relievers in relation to sleep health among African American women.
papers.abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVES: To investigate associations between religiosity/spirituality (R/S) and sleep along with potential modification by stress among Black/African American (AA) women. METHODS: Participants from the Study of Environment, Lifestyle, and Fibroids (2010-2018) reported importance of faith and R/S as a source of strength/comfort (ranging from "very" to "not at all") as well as frequency of prayer/meditation (ranging from "everyday", to "<once/month") at baseline. There were repeated measures of daily stress ("very high/moderate" vs. "low/none"), short sleep duration (<7 hours), non-restorative sleep (NRS, waking rested <4 days/week), and insomnia symptoms (IS; difficulty falling/staying asleep). Adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) were estimated with Poisson regression with robust variance, and adjusted risk ratios were estimated by applying generalized estimating equations to models. R/S-by-stress terms were tested. RESULTS: Among 1,693 Black/AA women (mean age ± SD 29.2 ± 3.4 years), 69.3% reported faith as important, 55.6% perceived R/S as a source of strength/comfort, 58.8% prayed/meditated daily, 43.8% reported high/moderate stress, and poor sleep was prevalent (short sleep:58.4%, NRS:62%, and IS:17.9%) at baseline. There were no associations with short sleep and IS. All three R/S measures were each cross-sectionally but not longitudinally associated with lower likelihood of NRS, however, associations differed by stress. R/S as source of strength/comfort and prayer/meditation showed protective associations with NRS prevalence at baseline only among participants with low versus high stress (e.g. prayer everyday vs. <once/month aPRhigh stress = 1.07 [95% CI: 0.91-1.26], aPRlow stress = 0.76 [95% CI: 0.63-0.91], pR/S*stress = 0.03). CONCLUSIONS: Higher R/S was associated with lower NRS prevalence, but protective associations were limited to participants with low/no reported stress. Statement of Significance Most Americans identify as religious or spiritual, yet religiosity/spirituality (R/S) remains an understudied determinant of sleep health despite its impact on health and well-being. Using multidimensional measures of R/S, we found that valuing faith, finding strength/comfort in R/S, and prayer/meditation were each associated with restorative sleep, primarily among those reporting low/no daily stress. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating R/S into culturally relevant sleep health research and interventions.

papers.title: Feasibility of implementing a mindfulness-based program for paediatric intensive care unit staff.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Paediatric intensive care unit (PICU) clinicians are particularly susceptible to workplace stress due to frequent ethical dilemmas (for example, perceptions of futile or unethical treatment), patient morbidity and mortality, sleep disruption, and emotional exhaustion, putting them at increased risk of anxiety, depression, and burnout. The psychological well-being of these healthcare professionals is vital for maintaining high standards of patient care and safety. OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility of implementing a mindfulness-based program among PICU staff, with a focus on acceptability and barriers to participation. METHODS: Weekly 20-min guided group-practice sessions in mindfulness, with both in-person and virtual attendance options, were held over a 6-month period. These sessions were offered to medical, nursing, and allied health staff working in the PICU of a specialist paediatric hospital in Queensland, Australia, serving families from Queensland and northern New South Wales. The program was offered during a period of increased personal and occupational stress arising from the delivery of high-acuity care during the global COVID-19 pandemic. FINDINGS: The program was successfully delivered within the PICU setting, with most participants expressing interest in continuation of the program (72%). Qualitative responses suggested perceived individual and collective well-being benefits, alongside generally positive perceptions of the program. However, participants also identified important barriers to participation, including workload pressures and rostering constraints. CONCLUSIONS: This study suggests that implementation of a mindfulness-based program within a PICU setting may be feasible while also highlighting important operational barriers to participation in high-acuity healthcare environments. Qualitative findings indicated generally positive staff perceptions and perceived acceptability of the program. Further research using longitudinal designs is recommended to better understand implementation considerations and potential longer-term outcomes associated with mindfulness-based interventions in PICU settings.
papers.journal: Australian critical care : official journal of the Confederation of Australian Critical Care Nurses

papers.title: Pilot, Feasibility, and Acceptability Evaluation of a Mindfulness-Based Intervention with Diabetes Education in Adolescents with Type 1 Diabetes.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Most adolescents living with type 1 diabetes (T1D) do not reach targeted levels of hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), which increases risk for diabetes-related complications. Suboptimal diabetes management may be associated with the burden of coping with T1D for adolescents who are simultaneously adjusting to physical, cognitive, and socioemotional changes. Mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) are associated with improved coping skills and could be useful for adolescents with T1D. METHODS: This was a pilot randomized controlled study to examine the feasibility and acceptability of a virtual MBI in adolescents aged 15-17 years with T1D. Enrollment took place in two iterations: 1) patients were approached in clinic by a physician; 2) letters were mailed and follow-up phone calls were made by research staff. Enrolled participants were given the option of 2 different weekly times for participation and were assigned to one of two study arms: diabetes education + MBI (DE+MBI) or DE only. For each arm, 12 virtual group sessions were held weekly. Feasibility measures included time-to-recruit, program enrollment, and study retention. Acceptability was assessed by attendance and survey completion. Exploratory outcomes included HbA1c and responses to quality of life and mental health questionnaires. RESULTS: By design, the first 60 eligible participants who agreed to participate were enrolled. Sixty of 164 approached (37%) consented to enroll. Fifty percent of these (n=30; DE+MBI=15, DE=15) participated in at least one group session; the mean attendance was 7 + 3 sessions. All participants reported managing at least one area of life better post-intervention (coping with stress, sleep, physical symptoms, self-care, school, emotion regulation, getting along with others). Survey completion was 87% pre-intervention and 60% post-intervention. There was no change in mean HbA1c for either the DE+MBI or the DE arms. CONCLUSION: More study is warranted to investigate ways to increase the feasibility for implementing complementary therapies such as MBI in a diabetes clinic for adolescents with T1D.
